strings.name: William Li
strings.summary: Li Bin, known as William Li, is a Chinese entrepreneur who worked in automotive internet services including Bitauto before founding NIO. He leads teams developing electric cars, battery swapping and battery subscriptions, with an emphasis on user communities. Products, networks and business models involve employees and partners.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Chair and CEO tenures, company and single-brand deliveries, listings by introduction and fundraising, signed agreements and completed closings are distinct. Assisted driving is not driverless operation.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded NIO and participated in automotive internet businesses, advancing electric vehicles, battery swapping and user-community business models.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Peking University sociology bachelor’s; 2026 commencement reporting identifies him as a 1996 graduate. The secondary-page law-degree claim is not used.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current and former offices
strings.facts.f2.value: NIO CEO since March 2018; Bitauto Holdings chairman from 2010 to 2020 and Dida director from 2015 to 2025. Uxin’s website still lists him as a director.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Vehicle-battery separation
strings.highlights.h1.text: Separates vehicle purchase from battery-use subscription, alongside swapping infrastructure. NIO, CATL and other partners established the battery asset company.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Automotive internet and users
strings.highlights.h2.text: Expanded from automotive information services into EVs and user communities. Participation does not make every user a direct shareholder or confer complete decision-making power.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Company reports October deliveries
strings.timeline.t1.text: Release records 34,246 vehicles across NIO, ONVO and FIREFLY; not NIO-brand-only deliveries or quarterly financial results.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Geely charging and swapping agreements
strings.timeline.t2.text: Company announces definitive agreements subject to regulatory and other closing conditions. Proposed ownership and later investment options are not completed outcomes.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Hong Kong and Singapore listings
strings.timeline.t3.text: Ordinary shares listed on March 10 and May 20 respectively. Both were secondary listings by introduction, not new-share fundraising through the listings themselves.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Launches BaaS battery subscription
strings.timeline.t4.text: Users can buy vehicles without batteries and subscribe for battery use. Launch rates are historical, not current prices.
strings.timeline.t5.title: NIO ADSs list on NYSE
strings.timeline.t5.text: Trading begins as NIO. Listing and company valuation are not founder wealth or cash proceeds.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes NIO CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Official biography and annual report date this tenure to March, separately from chairmanship since founding.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founds NIO as chairman
strings.timeline.t7.text: Company records November founding; teams later developed products, manufacturing partnerships and services, not all completed at inception.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-founds Bitauto business
strings.timeline.t8.text: Co-founded Beijing Bitauto E-Commerce; its early presidency is distinct from the later Bitauto Holdings chairmanship.
